finding.claim: Formula functions MUNIT and REPT size allocations directly from an untrusted formula argument with no upper bound, so one crafted cell formula can exhaust process memory.
finding.source: <f> formula text in an untrusted workbook, evaluated by CalcCellValue
finding.sink: MUNIT matrix allocation (calc.go:5258-5260) and REPT buffer loop (calc.go:14446-14448)

trace.note: evalInfixExpFunc takes function name from formula text
callFuncByName uses reflect MethodByName to dispatch to MUNIT/REPT
allocates N rows, each of N formulaArg
REPT reads repeat count from argument
REPT appends text N times with no cap

finding.guards_checked: Argument count and type checks; sign check (N<0 rejected) and zero short-circuit for REPT. No upper bound on N or resulting size, and no global cap in CalcCellValue.

finding.claim: The default UnzipSizeLimit is about 16.8 GB, and every non-worksheet zip part is fully read into memory up to that total, so a roughly 16 MB crafted xlsx can expand to roughly 16 GB of RAM (zip bomb).
finding.source: Zip central-directory declared sizes and compressed data in an untrusted .xlsx passed to OpenFile/OpenReader
finding.sink: readFile materializes each non-worksheet part in memory, pre-allocating the declared size

trace.note: non-worksheet parts go to readFile in memory

finding.guards_checked: Total declared-size cap (lib.go:33-41, 55-59) is enforced but the default is very large. Worksheets and sharedStrings above UnzipXMLSizeLimit are diverted to temp disk (lib.go:65-85), but other parts are not. Go zip reader caps real output at declared size. Operator can lower the limit via Options.UnzipSizeLimit.

finding.claim: Malformed encrypted-container headers cause unchecked slice bounds and index panics (standard and agile paths), crashing any host that opens an attacker-supplied encrypted workbook; the library has no recover().
finding.source: EncryptionInfo and EncryptedPackage CFB streams of an untrusted encrypted xlsx passed to Decrypt
finding.sink: Unchecked slicing and indexing in standardDecrypt, standardEncryptionVerifier, standardConvertPasswdToKey, agileDecrypt, convertPasswdToKey

trace.note: standardDecrypt reads encryptionInfoBuf[8:12] without length check
12+encryptionHeaderSize is uint32 and can wrap or exceed slice length
encryptedPackageBuf[8:] panics if stream missing or shorter than 8 bytes
x[bs:be] panics when ciphertext length is not a multiple of 16
agileDecrypt reads encryptionInfoBuf[8:] without length check
KeyEncryptor[0] panics when the XML has no key encryptor

finding.guards_checked: encryptionMechanism requires len>=4 (crypt.go:222); decryptPackage checks len(input)>=packageOffset (crypt.go:526); extractPart checks entry size against maxStreamSize (crypt.go:202). No recover() in non-test code. Other header fields are unchecked.

finding.claim: Formula dependency resolution recurses without any depth limit across distinct cells, so a long chain of formulas in a crafted workbook can exhaust the goroutine stack; Go stack overflow is a fatal, unrecoverable error. Plausible: depth at which the 1 GB stack is exhausted was not measured.
finding.source: Chain of distinct formula cells (A1=A2, A2=A3, ...) in an untrusted workbook evaluated by CalcCellValue
finding.sink: Unbounded recursion cellResolver -> calcCellValue -> evalInfixExp -> cellResolver

trace.note: revisit counter bounds re-entry into same cell only

finding.guards_checked: Per-cell revisit counter (calc.go:1824-1825) bounds repeated visits to the same cell, not depth across distinct cells. No depth limit found in calc.go (grep for depth/recurs returned none).

finding.claim: AMORDEGRC loop runs up to the formula-supplied period count when rate is zero, because nRate becomes zero and the early exit never triggers, allowing a CPU hang from one crafted formula.
finding.source: period and rate arguments of an AMORDEGRC formula in an untrusted workbook
finding.sink: Loop for n := 0; n < int(period.Number); n++ with no other exit

trace.note: rate rejected only if >= 0.5; zero accepted
early exit requires rest < 0, which never occurs when nRate is zero

finding.guards_checked: rate >= 0.5 check (calc.go:16356) only. No period upper bound and no iteration cap.

finding.claim: SetPanes indexes SheetView[len-1] after only a nil check, so an opened file with an empty non-nil <sheetViews> element causes index -1 and a panic; SetSelection at line 884 has the same unguarded index.
finding.source: Empty <sheetViews/> element in a worksheet of an untrusted file passed to OpenFile

trace.note: OpenFile loads worksheet with empty sheetViews
nil check only; empty non-nil slice passes

finding.guards_checked: Only nil check on ws.SheetViews (sheet.go:867). Length guard at sheet.go:872 comes after the panicking index at line 870. GetPanes at sheet.go:1019 does guard length.

finding.claim: The per-call MaxCalcIterations option passed to CalcCellValue is ignored by the cycle guard, which reads the file-level f.options value instead of ctx.maxCalcIterations. Logic flaw, not a security issue.
finding.source: Options.MaxCalcIterations passed to CalcCellValue by the caller

trace.note: ctx.maxCalcIterations declared and never read elsewhere

finding.guards_checked: Per-call value is stored but never consulted; no other use of ctx.maxCalcIterations found.
